## Trial `vlan-access-segmentation-rhel10__rrCsG8Q`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, before/after-restart evidence: node1's eth1 and eth2 are configured as untagged access ports in distinct VLANs (50 and 60) via a vlan-filtering bridge with per-VLAN SVIs, node2 and node3 each retain working connectivity to node1 within their own VLAN, and the two hosts remain mutually isolated (confirmed both by default behavior and by a deliberate attempt to route around the isolation, plus FDB evidence of no cross-VLAN MAC learning). The provider-wide restart protocol was executed for all three nodes with distinct pre/post boot IDs and recovered state, though on node1 a real reboot exposed that the IPv4-forwarding-disable sysctl did not survive reboot as originally configured; the executor diagnosed and fixed this by embedding the sysctl call in the persisted startup script, but the fix itself was only validated by a service restart rather than a second full reboot.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.880 | 0.850 | 59/6 (+4 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** node1's link to node2 (eth1) configured as an untagged access port in its own VLAN
  - **Why:** bridge vlan show confirms eth1 has vlan-id 50, PVID, Egress Untagged, both immediately after configuration (cmd-86e53da478664ada) and after node1's own restart (cmd-df112d5b6f4f4d76), demonstrating persistence.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-86e53da478664ada`, `cmd-df112d5b6f4f4d76`, `cmd-18eda3da25224377`, `cmd-64911d96462d403f`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** node1's link to node3 (eth2) configured as an untagged access port in its own VLAN, different from node2's
  - **Why:** bridge vlan show confirms eth2 has vlan-id 60, PVID, Egress Untagged, separate from eth1's VLAN 50, both at setup and after node1's restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-86e53da478664ada`, `cmd-df112d5b6f4f4d76`, `cmd-18eda3da25224377`, `cmd-64911d96462d403f`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** node2 keeps a working link to node1 inside its own VLAN
  - **Why:** node2 (192.168.50.2/24 on enp8s0, persisted via nmcli connection profile) successfully pings node1's SVI 192.168.50.1 before and after both node2's and node1's restarts.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0632a04fc5f64b6f`, `cmd-c34fc21a3de8466d`, `cmd-d74b0cb463de4216`, `cmd-df112d5b6f4f4d76`
- **R4 — Satisfied:** node3 keeps a working link to node1 inside its own VLAN
  - **Why:** node3 (192.168.60.3/24 on enp8s0, persisted via nmcli connection profile) successfully pings node1's SVI 192.168.60.1 before and after both node3's and node1's restarts.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ca6df100a1e64367`, `cmd-c34fc21a3de8466d`, `cmd-15465e36c5b14ab7`, `cmd-df112d5b6f4f4d76`
- **R5 — Satisfied:** node2 and node3 stay separated from one another (mutual isolation across VLANs)
  - **Why:** node2 cannot reach node3 by default ping, and even fails when an explicit static route via node1 is added (invalid gateway / 100% loss). bridge fdb on node1 shows eth1 only learns VLAN-50 MACs and eth2 only VLAN-60 MACs, confirming no cross-VLAN bridging. After node1's restart, isolation persists and is now explicitly attributed to disabled IPv4 forwarding, shown by a 'Destination Net Unreachable' ICMP response.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-cccd3560bd3b4350`, `cmd-d5cc8b1b05bf4440`, `cmd-665d9028b0e94d5d`, `cmd-2a12a8ad777c482e`, `cmd-df112d5b6f4f4d76`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.880**. Command trace shows disciplined, evidence-linked work. Early temporary IP assignments on eth1/eth2 (cmd-f8afe47967474cd5) and on node2/node3 enp8s0 (cmd-aea2bcb23db04a23, cmd-f98e331bf02b432d) were used only for link discovery and were removed shortly after (cmd-79bb418056c34833; node2/node3 addresses were already gone due to NetworkManager reverting non-profile changes, confirmed by cmd-97ba9ace11d74bf2/cmd-1a2468283cb14a89). A temporary static route added on node2 to more rigorously test isolation (cmd-cccd3560bd3b4350) was fully removed afterward (cmd-f33c45591fab4254) and directly supports the isolation requirement, so it is not an unnecessary mutation. Stopping and later restarting interfaces-config.service/networking.service on node1 (cmd-f4d00b9c5ee846df, cmd-6c0fc1e53ca8438b) was a necessary, bounded prerequisite for building the bridge and was restored. One genuine gap was caught and corrected: after node1's reboot, net.ipv4.conf.all.forwarding reverted to 1 because the sysctl.d file did not reliably apply to interfaces the oneshot unit created after boot (cmd-6add4e3c08dd4124, cmd-64911d96462d403f); the executor added an explicit sysctl -w call inside the persisted setup script (cmd-e47d55c225b84107) and re-verified forwarding=0, but this fix was validated only by restarting the service, not by a further full reboot cycle. Minor residue: a failed tcpdump attempt on node2 (cmd-92c74ce379f747c2, 'tcpdump: command not found') left an empty /tmp/t5.log file that persisted into the after-executor snapshot; this is trivial and did not affect functionality. Other diagnostic tcpdump logs on node1 were cleared by node1's own reboot (tmpfs).

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-f8afe47967474cd5`, `cmd-79bb418056c34833`, `cmd-aea2bcb23db04a23`, `cmd-f98e331bf02b432d`, `cmd-97ba9ace11d74bf2`, `cmd-1a2468283cb14a89`, `cmd-cccd3560bd3b4350`, `cmd-f33c45591fab4254`, `cmd-f4d00b9c5ee846df`, `cmd-6c0fc1e53ca8438b`, `cmd-6add4e3c08dd4124`, `cmd-64911d96462d403f`, `cmd-e47d55c225b84107`, `cmd-92c74ce379f747c2`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- The corrected forwarding-disable persistence fix on node1 (cmd-e47d55c225b84107) was validated only via 'systemctl restart vlan-access.service', not via an additional full reboot, so full confidence in its reboot-durability is not directly demonstrated.
- Executor's own final report claims 'proving changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery' but the raw timeline shows an intermediate failed recovery state on node1 (forwarding=1, vlan-access.service initially inactive) that was only resolved after manual intervention; this nuance is understated in the executor's summary.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.880); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.850; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
